The '''1968–69 season''' was the 70th completed season of [[The Football League]].

[[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] won the League for the first time in their history, finishing six points ahead of [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]. Newly promoted [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] were relegated after finishing bottom along with [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]].

Jim Hunter scored 22 goals including his 100th career goal in February 1969 against Coventry City

[[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] were runaway winners of the Second Division and they were joined in promotion by runners-up [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. Despite still boasting the talents of [[Johnny Haynes]] and [[George Cohen]], [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] finished bottom and were relegated. They were joined in the Third Division by perennial strugglers [[Bury F.C.|Bury]]

[[Watford F.C.|Watford]] won the Third Division title on goal average from [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] and both teams were duly promoted. At the bottom end [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]], [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool]], [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] and [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]] were all relegated.

The Fourth Division was won by [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]], who were promoted along with [[Halifax Town A.F.C.|Halifax Town]], [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] and [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]]. No team failed re-election so no new members were admitted to the [[The Football League|Football League]].

==Final league tables and results==

Beginning with the season 1894–95, clubs finishing level on points were separated according to goal average (goals scored divided by goals conceded), or more properly put, goal ratio. In case one or more teams had the same goal difference, this system favoured those teams who had scored fewer goals. The goal average system was eventually scrapped beginning with the 1976–77 season.<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1968-69.html |title=England 1968-69 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=2010-02-24}}</ref>

Since the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] was established in the [[1958–59 Football League|1958–59 season]], the bottom four teams of that division have been required to apply for [[re-election (Football League)|re-election]].<ref name="Rothmans">Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane's, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref>

*With thirteen minutes remaining in the Barrow v Plymouth Argyle match on the 9th of November 1968, the score was 0-0. After Barrow took a corner-kick, the ball was cleared towards Barrow player George Mclean. His shot from outside the penalty area was going wide, but hit referee Ivan Robinson and went into the net. Robinson had no choice but to award the goal. Barrow held on to win 1-0.<ref name="Ward">{{cite book |last1=Ward |first1=Andrew |title=Football's Strangest Matches: Extraordinary but true stories from over a century of football |date=2010 |publisher=Portico |location=London |isbn=1907554084 |pages=87}}</ref>
